entries.text:
Task: harden how toolreader displays Codex sessions, testing against the real Codex CLI sessions on this machine. Report back what you found and fixed.

Context: toolreader (this repo, read AGENTS.md first and follow it exactly, including "The ways to hurt yourself") is a read-only viewer of what coding agents did. It already lists and renders Codex sessions that ran outside T3 through `codex app-server` (src/server/CodexSessions.ts, src/core/codex.ts, src/core/normalize.ts). There are ~2600 Codex rollout files under <path>

Branch: you are on `feat/production-plan`. Create `fix/codex-display` from it and commit there. Do not touch master or push anything.

What to do:
1. Pick ~15 diverse real Codex sessions (interactive CLI, `codex exec`, long ones, ones with apply_patch / file edits, MCP tool calls, web search, failed commands, subagents, images, very large outputs, old and new rollout formats). For each, compare what the viewer shows (API `/api/threads/<id>` and the UI) against the raw rollout JSONL. Look for: missing or duplicated actions, wrong kinds/colors, wrong status (failed shown as ok), broken diffs, wrong timestamps/order, unreadable titles, items that degrade to untyped rows, crashes, slow loads.
2. Fix what is wrong, at the root cause, each with a focused unit test using a trimmed, anonymized payload (no real secrets or private paths in fixtures).
3. Known bug to fix too: shell commands quoted like '"'…'"' are parsed wrongly in src/core/shell.ts.
4. Run the server on PORT=4779 (never 4777) against a snapshot of the T3 DB as AGENTS.md "Test data" describes. Use the T3 preview browser tools to check the UI for the sessions you fixed. Stop only the server PID you started.
5. Verify: `vp test run`, `vp check`, `vp run typecheck`, `vp run build`. Commit in small conventional commits (git -c user.email=<private> commit), each ending with the line: Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Report: a table of sessions checked (id prefix, kind, what was wrong), the commits you made, and anything you found but did not fix.

It looks like the formatter changed rollout.test.ts after the fix check ran, so the formatted version got committed anyway — I should verify git status is clean. I also want to check the UI for the code-mode session 019f4c03 and the old 0.42 session 01998862, plus grab one more screenshot of 019f4c03.

entries.text:
I'm putting together a report with a session table of roughly 16 sessions, comparing action counts before and after the fix. For example, one CLI session went from 0 to 13 tool executions, while a desktop code-mode session jumped from 60 to 105 visible actions once 82 previously-invisible exec scripts were accounted for.

Going through each session: several jump from 0 actions to dozens (15, 87, 95, 38, 62, 43, 21, 28), one massive compacted session with write_stdin merging shows 0 to 260, and a couple sessions like the codex-tui one stay flat at 64 since they already tracked command execution correctly with no duplicates. I'm also noting fixes like web searches and subagent spawns not being double-counted, untyped image generation rows getting properly named, and interrupted calls that previously got stuck showing "running" forever now correctly marked as failed.

Tallying up the before-counts more precisely for the larger sessions, I realize there are still gaps not addressed: 31 of the oldest rollouts from August 2025 aren't being listed by the app-server at all, and code-mode scripts that build commands in loops don't get properly expanded into individual tool items.

Other unresolved edge cases include MCP failures from rollout-only calls lacking error flags so they appear to succeed, shell keywords producing odd parsed titles, the heuristic nature of rolled-back-turn filtering potentially misattributing parallel scripts, and heredoc-based apply_patch calls showing up as generic shell runs. Also noting that CLAUDE's instruction to ask before opening browsers doesn't apply here since the user explicitly instructed it.

I fixed the Codex display and committed seven commits on `fix/codex-display`; nothing was pushed and master is untouched. The biggest problem was that about 83% of Codex tool calls never reached the viewer: 270 sessions showed no actions at all.

**Why the calls were missing:** `codex app-server thread/read` only rebuilds items from `item_completed` events in the rollout. Most rollouts only record those for messages and reasoning. Commands, patches, MCP calls, web searches and subagent calls exist only as plain tool-call lines in the file (about 29k of 35.7k calls across 1374 listed sessions). The server already reads each rollout file for timestamps, so the new `src/core/rollout.ts` picks up those calls in the same pass and turns them into the same item shapes. Calls that `thread/read` already returns are not shown twice.

**Final checks:** `vp test run` (89 passing), `vp check`, `vp run typecheck` and `vp run build` all pass. I ran every one of the 1487 Codex threads and 223 T3 threads through the API against a snapshot of the T3 database: no errors, none slower than 2s, all in time order. The largest file (46 MB) loads in 0.18s. In the UI I checked `019c42ae` (swimlane, failed commands with exit codes, a recovered patch shown as a diff) and `019f4c03` (scripts mixed in time order with the MCP calls they made). I stopped only my own server (PID 40532) and confirmed port 4779 is free.

### Sessions checked
The 0.10x–0.15x versions are newer than 0.4x–0.9x. "Before" counts are the tool items `thread/read` returned.

| Session | Kind | What was wrong | Actions before → after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `01998862` | CLI 0.42, `shell` with an argv list | no actions; JSON outputs and sandbox denials not read | 0 → 15 |
| `0199bf01` | CLI 0.45, `apply_patch` + shell | no actions or diffs | 0 → 87 |
| `019b2787` | CLI 0.73, `shell_command` | no actions | 0 → 43 |
| `019b46c5` | CLI 0.77 | no actions; an `rg` that found nothing shown as failed | 0 → 13 |
| `019ba913` | CLI 0.80, compacted, 88 `write_stdin` | no actions; long-running commands lost their later output | 0 → 260 (stdin output merged into its command) |
| `019be764` | `codex exec` 0.87 | no actions | 0 → 21 |
| `019cd860` | `codex exec`, `view_image` | no actions | 0 → 62 |
| `019c42ae` | Desktop 0.99: commands, 28 patches, web | no actions; patch hunks without line numbers drawn as whole-file adds | 0 → 95 |
| `019e1be8-d638` | web searches | no actions | 0 → 28 |
| `019dab33` | codex-tui 0.121 | already complete; checked nothing is doubled | 64 → 64 |
| `019e6a48` | Desktop, `<organization>` MCP | MCP results shown as raw JSON | 22 → 32 |
| `019ead39` | context7 MCP + web | most calls missing | 30 → 114 |
| `019ecfef` | 14 subagents | no subagent actions | 0 → 38 |
| `019ecb11` | 32 web searches + subagents | most calls missing | 36 → 143 |
| `019f4c03` | Desktop 0.144 script ("code mode") `exec` | 82 scripts invisible; `bun -e` script labelled "setup" | 60 → 105 (plan-only scripts skipped) |
| `019f7b72` | largest file, 46 MB | most calls missing | ~249 → 351 |
| `019f8513` | image generation | rows titled just `imageGeneration` | now named from the image prompt |

### Commits
1. `856d133 fix(shell): unquote sh -c scripts the way the shell does` — the known `'"'…'"'` bug. It also fixes `rg "a\.b"` losing its backslash.
2. `60b75c9 fix(shell): bun -e <code> is a run, not an install`
3. `263abf4 fix(shell): keep $(…) and backtick substitutions inside their word` — titles like `-n 1 f)` are gone, and `command -v x` now shows as `which x`.
4. `fb368cc fix(normalize): searches that found nothing no longer show as failed` — Codex marks `rg` exit 1 as failed. This dropped failed searches from 361 to 176; the rest are real errors.
5. `3481516 fix(codex): show the tool calls thread/read drops` — the main fix. A call left without output in an interrupted turn shows as failed instead of spinning forever.
6. `8b30818 fix(codex): name image generation and scripted image views`
7. `0e01fd1 fix(normalize): blank lines in apply_patch hunks no longer skew the diff` — I found this one while checking the UI.

Each commit has a focused test with made-up paths and data.

### Found but not fixed
- **Oldest rollouts not listed:** 31 rollouts from August 2025, in the oldest format, aren't returned by `thread/list`, so they never appear. Showing them would need a second reader.
- **Scripts that loop over commands:** scripts that build commands in a loop (`const cmds=[…]`) show as one "script …" row. Script rows only report the script's own success or failure, not each command's exit code.
- **MCP failures:** MCP calls recovered from the rollout have no error flag in their output, so they show as ok even if they failed.
- **Shell keywords in titles:** `for/do`, `case`, `[[ ]]` and `{ }` still produce odd title parts.
- **Rare cases:** `apply_patch <<PATCH` run through the shell shows as a command rather than an edit. Recovered patches have no real line numbers, so the viewer hides them.
- **Heuristics:** skipping a script whose calls `thread/read` already shows is based on line position, so parallel scripts could be mixed up. Calls from rolled-back turns are only dropped when the turn ids match on both sides.

I wrote a before/after diff of the actions view to `<path>` (98 KB). It compares the base commit (`5264d6d`) with `fix/codex-display` (`0e01fd1`) across the 17 sessions I checked.

Both versions read the same `thread/read` output and the same rollout files, so the only difference is the code. Each action appears as `status kind title`; timestamps are left out so rows that only moved don't count as changes. Across the 17 sessions the view goes from **509 to 1,568 actions**.

Most sessions go from **0 actions to a full list** (e.g. `019ba913`: 0 → 260). Sessions that already had items show the real changes: `019f4c03` gains 45 previously hidden code-mode script actions with no duplicates, and `019dab33` (my control session) shows no change.

Four verified defects at `0e01fd1`. All affect the displayed session history.

- **P2: The merge drops separate web actions that use the same query or URL.** [src/core/codex.ts:221](./src/core/codex.ts:221)
  - Failing input: `thread/read` contains search `ws1` for `"effect schema"`. The rollout contains a later search `ws2` for the same query. Only `ws1` remains. An `open_page` also removes a later `find_in_page` for that URL.
  - What I'd do here is match individual calls by ID. Where IDs differ, match one occurrence using the action type, arguments, and position. A query or URL alone cannot identify a call.

  ```text
  Search ws1 + later search ws2 → only ws1
  ```

- **P2: A failed command inside a completed script shows as `ok`.** [src/core/rollout.ts:403](./src/core/rollout.ts:403)
  - Failing input: script `text(await tools.exec_command({cmd: "pnpm test"}));`, followed by `Script completed\nOutput:\n{"exit_code":1,"output":"1 test failed"}`. With no nested item from `thread/read`, the viewer shows `pnpm test` as `ok`, with no exit code.
  - The code checks whether the script failed. It does not check the command result. Decode known command result shapes with Schema and preserve their exit codes. Keep a script action when command status cannot be recovered.

  ```text
  Command exits 1 → script completes → command shown as ok
  ```

- **P2: Initial output marks a running command as successful.** [src/core/rollout.ts:342](./src/core/rollout.ts:342)
  - Failing input: `exec_command` runs `pnpm build` and returns `Process running with session ID 41\nOutput:\nbuilding\n`. The viewer shows `ok` while the turn is active. It also shows `ok` after an interrupted turn with no final result.
  - The fix is to track completion separately from output. A session or cell ID means the call is still running. Set the final status when its continuation finishes or the turn is interrupted.

  ```text
  Partial output + session ID → outputs.length > 0 → ok
  ```

- **P2: An escaped quote in a substitution hides later command parts.** [src/core/shell.ts:167](./src/core/shell.ts:167)
  - Failing input: `TOKEN=[redacted] "a\"b") && git push`. This is valid shell syntax. `humanizeCommand` returns `[]`; the parser treats the rest of the command as part of the assignment.
  - `indexOf` treats the escaped quote as the closing quote. What I'd do here is scan quoted text with escape handling, then resume substitution parsing at the correct position.

  ```text
  Escaped quote → wrong closing quote → git push swallowed
  ```

The three focused test files pass: **19 tests**. The inputs above reproduce failures those tests do not cover. A synthetic 53 MB rollout with 5,000 calls scanned in about **121 ms**. I found no verified serious performance or catastrophic regex issue. The checkout stayed unchanged.

entries.text:
Only about 18% of scripts print the full decodable result JSON with exit codes, while 82% just print raw output with unknown status. So I should decode known result shapes and preserve their exit codes, but fall back to showing an undetermined-status case as a script action rather than a command when status can't be recovered.

But applying that broadly would turn most code-mode commands into generic "script" rows with ugly titles like the raw exec_command call, losing the nice humanized read/search titles — that's a real readability tradeoff. The domain also has no "unknown" status to fall back on, so adding one would ripple into the UI. Since the reviewer explicitly suggested keeping it as a script action when status is unrecoverable, I could make that script action's title still reflect the actual command (e.g. "script: sed -n '1,240p' SKILL.md") so it's honest about completion status while staying readable.

Still, the kind would be "tool" rather than read/search, shifting the swimlane color — a tradeoff I'll flag in the report. The core concern remains: showing a failed command as "ok" is actively misleading, like a failed pnpm test displaying success. The principled fix is to recover the exit code wherever possible and mark status as failed when it's non-zero, falling back to the script-row approach only when no exit code can be recovered at all.

For multi-command scripts, I'll try decoding known JSON shapes — either a single object with exit_code or an array of result objects — and take the first nonzero exit code if any exist, otherwise 0. Text conventions like "exit=0" embedded in output I'll leave alone since those are printing styles, not structured shapes, and I only want to decode via schema. When decoding succeeds, I'll also simplify the displayed output to just the joined inner `output` fields rather than raw JSON, though I need to watch for cases where truncation has cut off the JSON before it can even parse.

For deduplicating web search calls, I'm matching by ID where possible, but for items without matching rollout call IDs I need to pair them up using the action type, query/url arguments, and position — building a lookup of unmatched thread items keyed by type and query, then for each web_search_call looking for an unconsumed item whose line appears shortly after (within about 5 lines) and consuming it once matched.

I need a normalization key that works across both shapes, falling back through query, pattern, or queries[0] when the primary field is missing, and I should extend the action schema to optionally include pattern and queries fields so this stays consistent.

I'm working out a dedup key: for search actions use the query text, for open_page use the URL, and include pattern for find_in_page too, excluding query for plain page opens. I also need to normalize action type naming since the rollout format uses snake_case like "open_page" but the app-server layer likely converts it to camelCase, so I should account for that conversion when matching types.

Now I'm writing the logic to find where a shell command substitution ends, handling backticks, single quotes, double quotes with escape sequences, and nested `$(...)` substitutions recursively.

I realize there's an edge case: the tokenizer's own double-quote parsing doesn't handle nested `$(...)` containing quotes, like `"$(printf "x")"`. A fix would be to detect `$(` inside that branch and delegate to the substitution-aware scanner too, so nested quotes inside command substitutions don't break the outer quote parsing.

Now I want to draft tests for this: one verifying `TOKEN=[redacted] "a\"b") && git push` tokenizes correctly, and another checking that nested substitutions inside double quotes resolve properly for a file write case. Before writing them, I should check the existing rollout test file to confirm the current helper names since the file may have changed.



Around 18% of code-mode scripts print the full `exec_command` JSON result (including exit code), while the remaining 82% only print `r.output`, making exit code unrecoverable for those. Next I'll review the current test helpers, then write the four failing tests first.
